question.problem:
Consider the vector space $\text{M}_2(\mathbb{R})$ of all $2 \times 2$ matrices over $\mathbb{R}.$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14151605/assets/e98eb00ac7ee6ffb83d4a902d92e9bda4434e6bfaeae1fb91a210849d3e1991f.svg) is a linearly independent set in $\text{M}_2(\mathbb{R})$

II. $[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]$ can be expressed as a linear combination of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14151605/assets/716877f60112610eae19b094ca691edf0c0d2ecdffc54dc0b785d66c96e64909.svg)

III. ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14151605/assets/ccd021603e72ceb60be92eabec243bfdd5ce33eb22a6b801030a05efc02a861d.svg) is a basis of $\text{M}_2(\mathbb{R})$
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, the equation
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14151605/assets/a16ee652347a67e66994875711dff835418bfcfb4f85a058a80f9164af525cab.svg)
is true if and only if $x_1=x_2=0.$ So, the set is linearly independent.

- Statement II is true. Indeed,
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14151605/assets/f173928232bbfd7680c2952250c78e7ba354bd4851cb4783bd531cc683044db5.svg)

- Statement III is false. For example, the matrix $[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]$ can't be written as a linear combination of 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14151605/assets/7449707a6aa218f65cc22db3a56e8ed9391e3b5e562301e77fd62cb2f3dad20a.svg)
since all these linear combinations result in matrices with the entry $a_{11} = 0\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14151605/assets/b952b253393b4d14572b41ad1ca265e3b858edeec36e4c937f644621ae497294.svg)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
